suite: EMS Commercial Legal Frozen Regression Corpus v0.3
purpose: Frozen synthetic regression cases for source-grounded EMS issue spotting. These cases are not approved negotiation standards and must not be used as precedent.

cases.title: Forecast procurement without recovery
cases.text: Supplier may purchase material against Customer's twelve-week forecast. Customer may reduce or cancel forecasts at any time. Supplier shall be solely responsible for all excess, obsolete, non-cancelable and non-returnable material.
mustNotConclude: customer is obligated to purchase the inventory

cases.title: Convenience termination without material recovery
cases.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience on thirty days' notice. On termination Customer will pay only for conforming finished goods delivered before the termination effective date.

cases.title: Net 90 payment terms
cases.text: Payment terms are Net 90 from receipt of a correct invoice.

cases.title: Unlimited liability and lost profits
cases.text: Supplier's liability shall be unlimited. The exclusion of consequential damages does not apply to Customer's lost profits, lost revenue, recall costs or loss of business.

cases.title: Five-year design-inclusive warranty
cases.text: Supplier warrants that Products will meet all Customer requirements and intended use for sixty months after shipment, including defects arising from Customer design specifications.

cases.title: Firm pricing without external-cost relief
cases.text: Prices are firm and fixed for the term and will not be adjusted for tariff increases, foreign exchange movement, commodity increases, labor cost changes or changes in law.

cases.title: Express SOW-over-MSA conflict
cases.text: The MSA states payment is Net 45. This SOW states payment is Net 90 and provides that the SOW controls over conflicting terms in the MSA.

cases.title: Operational meetings do not amend agreement
cases.text: The parties will meet quarterly to review operational performance. Meeting minutes are informational and do not amend this Agreement unless signed by authorized representatives of both parties.
mustNotConclude: quarterly meeting creates a purchase obligation

cases.title: Binding forecast window
cases.text: The first eight weeks of each rolling forecast are binding and authorize Supplier to procure components and capacity. Weeks nine through sixteen are planning estimates only.

cases.title: PO boilerplate precedence risk
cases.text: Each purchase order is subject to Customer's then-current purchasing terms. In the event of conflict, the terms printed on the purchase order prevail over this Agreement.

cases.title: Customer recovery for authorized NCNR
cases.text: Customer shall purchase at Supplier's landed cost all non-cancelable and non-returnable components reasonably procured in reliance on Customer's binding forecast, subject to Supplier's documented mitigation efforts.

cases.title: Consigned inventory loss allocation
cases.text: Customer retains title to all consigned material. Supplier bears risk of loss for consigned material only while the loss results from Supplier's negligence or willful misconduct.

cases.title: Finished goods title before payment
cases.text: Title to finished Products transfers to Customer upon completion of final acceptance testing at Supplier's facility. Risk of loss transfers only upon delivery FCA Supplier facility.

cases.title: Unfunded safety stock
cases.text: Supplier shall maintain eight weeks of safety stock at its sole cost. Customer has no obligation to purchase safety stock that becomes excess or obsolete.

cases.title: Customer ECO without cost recovery
cases.text: Customer may require engineering changes at any time. Supplier shall implement each change immediately without adjustment to price, lead time, inventory liability or delivery commitments.

cases.title: Open-ended acceptance
cases.text: Customer may reject Products for any nonconformity discovered at any time, notwithstanding prior inspection, acceptance, use or payment. No time limit applies to rejection rights.

cases.title: DDP obligation with tariff exposure
cases.text: Supplier shall deliver all Products DDP Customer's facility and is responsible for all freight, customs duties, tariffs, taxes and import formalities without price adjustment.

cases.title: Broad product indemnity including customer design
cases.text: Supplier shall indemnify Customer from all claims arising from the Products, including claims caused by Customer-provided specifications, designs, instructions or modifications.
mustNotConclude: indemnity is limited to supplier fault

cases.title: Low annual-fees liability cap
cases.text: Supplier's aggregate liability arising out of this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid to Supplier during the three months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

cases.title: Force majeure without supply allocation rules
cases.text: Neither party is liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control. During a force majeure event Supplier must continue to prioritize Customer above all other customers without additional charge.
mustNotConclude: supplier may allocate supply pro rata

cases.title: Supplier absorbs regulatory changes
cases.text: Supplier is responsible for all costs resulting from any new or changed law, regulation, tariff, environmental requirement or governmental order affecting manufacture or delivery of Products.

cases.title: Absolute sustainability warranty
cases.text: Supplier warrants that every tier of its supply chain will at all times comply with Customer's sustainability code, achieve Customer's annual emissions targets and provide complete traceability for all raw materials.
mustNotConclude: obligation is limited to commercially reasonable efforts

cases.title: Forecast termination E&O interaction
cases.text: Customer's twelve-week forecast authorizes Supplier to place non-cancelable material orders. Customer may terminate for convenience on fifteen days' notice. Upon termination Customer purchases only finished Products already accepted before the termination date.

cases.title: Payment setoff and disputed invoices
cases.text: Invoices are payable Net 60. Customer may withhold or set off any amount it reasonably believes may become payable by Supplier under any agreement between the parties, including unliquidated or disputed claims.
mustNotConclude: only undisputed amounts may be withheld
